sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r10/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: 'Quality Checks' row 43 (scoring.toml gates zero the reward and skip the scored suite, gates carry no weight, and the functional floor stops a non-working app farming polish/visual) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 43 annotation (Gate/constraint failures hard-zero the quality terms, and passing only the cheap gates earns little); 'Deterministic Checks' check-scoring-policy.py row; also rows 21/24/42 for context
.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r10/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (delivery profile: shaped 0.6/0.2/0.2 behind two zero-weight gates and a functional floor)
evidence: Mechanics verified from source and by executing an unmodified copy of the frozen score.py+scoring.toml in the scratchpad (outside the workspace) on synthetic RewardKit outputs. (1) task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is byte-identical to the template: [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2; [floors] functional = 0.05. Gates appear only in [gates], never in [weights], so they hold no reward mass. (2) score.py:40-48 (identical to template): gates_passed = all(score > 0.0); scored dims are forced to 0.0 unless gates_passed and scored reward.json exists; reward = weighted only if gates_passed and floors_passed (functional > 0.05), else 0.0; returns exit 1 on gate failure. (3) test.sh:212-227 (identical to template): rm -rf scored dir, run gates suite, score.py; exit status 1 -> 'exit 0' (scored suite never launched, gate-failure record kept), other non-zero -> write_zero_reward; scored suite only after exit 0; any scored-suite or second score.py failure leaves/writes reward 0. (4) Both gate judge.toml files use aggregation = "all_pass" with one binary criterion (render:15-21, constraints:15-21), so a gate score is 0 or 1; gate prompts map evaluator failure to binary 0 (render prompt.md:11, constraints prompt.md:11). Gates are meaningful against dead apps: hro_gate_shared demands a UI-created job+candidate read back by the Observer in an independent context and rejects static seed/no-op/browser-only saves. Each scored prompt restates the same in-dimension browser gate (functional prompt.md:11-13 binary 0; polish prompt.md:29-30 binary 0; visual prompt.md:11-12 Likert 1 = normalized 0). Simulation results: gate render 0 + perfect scored -> reward 0.0000, exit 1; gates pass + functional 0.0342 (2.0/58.5) + perfect polish/visual -> reward 0.0000 (floors_passed 0, weighted 0.4205 discarded); gates pass + scored suite missing -> 0.0000; gates pass + functional 1/polish 0/visual 0 -> 0.6. Floor arithmetic: functional total weight 58.5 over 43 binary criteria, so the floor requires > 2.925 weight points. A gate-only app (job+candidate shared storage, seed loaded, survives restart) can plausibly earn hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_restart 1.5 = 2.0 (0.034) -> floor stops it from farming polish/visual. Conforming alternative check: a strong app that fails no gate is not penalized by gates; gate criteria explicitly leave stage rules, conversations and live updates to scored rows, so no stronger app is gated out for scored-only behaviour. Observation (not a confirmed defect, recorded for rows 42/44 reconciliation): an intake-only app that adds field validation (hro_job_open 0.5, hro_add_candidate 0.5, hro_add_email_rules 1, hro_restart 1.5 = 3.5 -> 0.0598) clears the 0.05 floor with no board moves, conversations, live updates or activity; with polish 0 and a well-styled visual 0.75 it would score about 0.186 (simulated). That app genuinely works for intake, the floor value is template-controlled, and 0.186 is far below a full app, so this is 'earns little' rather than a non-working app farming craft. Risk=true because raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent': no measured run shows the real RewardKit gate output keys/all_pass values flowing through test.sh, nor a mutated weak app actually zeroed by gate/floor under the configured judge. Source and synthetic simulation are not that measurement.
